paragraphs: Friend, here's the whole song in one breath: "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want" (Psalm 23:1). Everything after that line is David showing what it looks like to have that shepherd. Rest, water, a restored soul and guidance all come from Him (Psalm 23:2-3). FULL. SERVICE. SHEPHERD.

Here's what makes the song so honest: the good days and the hard days have the same shepherd. In the valley of the shadow of death, David says, "I will fear no evil, for You are with me" (Psalm 23:4). At a table "in the presence of my enemies," his cup still overflows (Psalm 23:5). I think the comfort isn't that the hard places disappear, friend. It's that the shepherd is in them.

And that care doesn't run out. David says, "Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever" (Psalm 23:6). So the big idea is this: when the LORD is your shepherd, you lack nothing, you're never alone in the dark places, and your whole life ends up at home with Him.
